title: Best Smart Dehumidifier (2026): Alexa, Google & App Picks
h1: The Best Smart Dehumidifiers for Voice Control, Alerts and Automations
dek: A smart dehumidifier should do more than show a number on your phone. These pick up voice commands, warn you before trouble starts and fit into the routines you already run.
description: The best smart dehumidifier for Alexa, Google Assistant and app alerts, from Midea, GE, Honeywell, GoveeLife and Dreo, compared on pumps, automations and real use.
intro: A **smart dehumidifier** earns its keep in places you don't visit every day: a basement, a lake house, the far end of a finished lower level. The best ones let you change the humidity target by voice, ping your phone before the tank fills or the coil freezes, and slot into a bedtime or away-from-home routine. Our top pick, the **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump**, pairs app control with a built-in pump that sends its own water away, so the app becomes the only thing you need to check.

If you're shopping for one, three things matter more than the spec sheet. First, **which ecosystem** you live in: Alexa, Google Assistant or just the brand's app. Second, **drainage**, because a smart unit that stops every day with a full bucket isn't saving you any trips. Third, **useful alerts**: full-tank, filter and fault notifications are worth more than a pretty humidity graph. Everything below is judged on those three, plus DOE-rated capacity and efficiency.
topPicksLead: The **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump** is our top smart dehumidifier because it pairs app, Alexa and Google Assistant control with a built-in pump, an ENERGY STAR rating and coverage up to 4,500 square feet, so it can run all season without you.

It works with the Midea app, Alexa and Google Assistant, so it fits whichever speaker you already own, and the built-in pump lifts water to a utility sink or out a window instead of waiting for you to empty a bucket.

The rest of the lineup is in our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If voice control is the point, this GE covers both major assistants and pairs them with GE's SmartHQ app for 24-hour schedules. Smart Dry trims the fan speed as the room dries, and auto restart means a power blip doesn't leave it sitting idle while you're away.

There's no pump: water collects in a 15-pint bucket that shuts the unit off with a 10-second alarm when full, or drains through a gravity hose you supply. Auto defrost keeps it working in cool basements. More GE options are in our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide.
products.notes: Buy a standard garden-style drain hose and put the unit above a floor drain if you want it to run unattended.

sections.heading: Smart vs. Wi-Fi dehumidifier: what's the difference?

blocks.text: Every model here connects to Wi-Fi, but "smart" should mean more than remote on/off. Our [best Wi-Fi dehumidifier](/best/best-wifi-dehumidifier/) guide covers app control in general. This one is narrower: whether a dehumidifier answers to a voice assistant, sends alerts you'd act on, runs on a schedule and plays well with other devices.

items.label: Voice assistants most smart dehumidifiers support: Alexa and Google Assistant
The Wi-Fi band most appliance-grade dehumidifiers require
A sensible setpoint for most basements and living spaces

blocks.text: We don't run a lab. We compare capacity under the 2019 DOE test procedure, ENERGY STAR listings and manufacturer manuals, then read each brand's app and voice-assistant documentation to see what you can actually control. Owner reviews tell us which apps drop their connection and which units forget their settings after a power blip.

For this guide we weighted voice-assistant support and useful notifications highest, followed by drainage that lets the unit run unattended, rated capacity and efficiency. Every pick is a verified Amazon listing.

sections.heading: How to choose a smart dehumidifier

items.label: Match your voice assistant
items.text: Check the listing for Alexa, Google Assistant or both. Apple HomeKit and Matter support are still rare on dehumidifiers, so don't assume them.

items.label: Size it first, connect it second
items.text: No app fixes an undersized unit. A bedroom needs about 20–22 pints; a damp basement 35–50. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the full chart.

items.label: Plan the drainage
items.text: A pump or gravity hose is what turns remote control into hands-off control. Compare self-draining units in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

items.label: Look for alerts you'd act on
items.text: Full-tank, filter, defrost and fault notifications are the useful ones.
sub: Full-tank or pump-fault alerts prevent days of downtime
Filter reminders keep airflow and efficiency up
Energy tracking shows what each setpoint costs

items.label: Confirm auto-restart
items.text: A smart unit that powers back up in standby after an outage is no help when you're away. Check the manual for auto-restart with saved settings.

items.label: Use a setpoint, not Continuous
items.text: Let the humidistat cycle the compressor. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

sections.heading: What you can automate (and what you can't)

blocks.text: Voice assistants handle the basics well: turn it on, change the target, switch modes. The bigger win is routines. A few that owners find genuinely useful:

items: **Bedtime routine:** drop the fan speed or turn off a living-room unit when you say good night, then raise it again in the morning.

**Off-peak schedule:** run harder overnight when electricity is cheaper. Our guide to [how much electricity a dehumidifier uses](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) shows why this matters on a 500-plus kWh-a-year machine.
**Away mode:** raise the setpoint a few points while you travel, then lower it before you return.

blocks.text: Every dehumidifier measures humidity at its own intake, which is often the driest air in the room. A separate Wi-Fi hygrometer at the far end of the space gives you an independent alert if conditions drift. See our [best hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/) picks.

blocks.title: What smart features can't do
blocks.text: No app makes a 22-pint unit dry a wet basement, and no alert empties a bucket. Smart features save trips and catch problems early; capacity and drainage still do the actual work.

sections.heading: Which smart dehumidifier should you buy?

items: **You want one machine for a basement below the nearest drain:** the **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump**.
**You want Alexa or Google voice control and have a floor drain:** the **GE 50-Pint Wi-Fi**.
**Your home already runs on Govee sensors or lights:** the **GoveeLife with Pump**.
**You want the lowest running cost in a medium basement:** the **Honeywell TP50AWKNR**, an ENERGY STAR Most Efficient model with Alexa and Google.
**You care most about running costs in a living space:** the **Dreo 75** and its energy monitor.
**It's a single bedroom or office:** the **Midea 22-Pint Smart**.
**It's a second home:** read our [vacation home dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-vacation-home/) guide for auto-restart and remote-monitoring advice.

blocks.text: The **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump** is the smart dehumidifier most people should buy: both major voice assistants, a pump that keeps it running, and an ENERGY STAR rating at a full 50 pints. Choose the **GE 50-Pint Wi-Fi** for voice control without a pump where a floor drain is handy, the **Honeywell TP50AWKNR** for the most efficient smart option, the **GoveeLife with Pump** if you live in Govee's app, and the **Midea 22-Pint Smart** for one room. Whatever you choose, set a humidity target and let the alerts do the watching.

faqs.q: Is a smart dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, if the unit lives somewhere you don't see every day, like a basement or second home. Alerts and remote control save trips and catch full tanks or faults early. For a bedroom you walk past daily, a basic model with a good humidistat does the same drying for less.

faqs.q: Which smart dehumidifiers work with Alexa and Google Assistant?
faqs.a: Among our picks, the Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump, the GE 50-Pint Wi-Fi and the Honeywell TP50AWKNR list both. The Midea 22-Pint Smart lists Alexa, the GoveeLife lists voice control through its app, and Dreo doesn't list voice-assistant support for the 75-pint model.

faqs.q: Is the Midea 50-pint smart dehumidifier with pump worth the extra money?
faqs.a: If there's no floor drain lower than the unit, yes. It's rated at the same 50 pints a day as Midea's gravity-drain models, so the premium buys mainly the pump — but that pump is what lets it run all season without anyone emptying it. Note that it's a standard upright tower, not the collapsible Cube.

faqs.q: Is the GE 50-pint smart dehumidifier any good?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want voice control. The GE 50-Pint Wi-Fi works with Alexa, Google Assistant and the SmartHQ app, adds Smart Dry and auto restart, and covers up to 5,000 square feet. It has no pump, though, so pair it with a floor drain and a hose, or choose GE's pump model, which skips Wi-Fi.

faqs.q: What happens to a smart dehumidifier when the Wi-Fi goes down?
faqs.a: It keeps running on its last settings using its own humidistat; you just lose remote control and alerts until the connection returns. A power outage is the bigger risk, so confirm the model auto-restarts with saved settings.
